notes:
Background: PrismFlow runs real-time inference for heterogeneous edge clients (ad bidding + content moderation). They need reserved capacity for predictable latency during peak ad cycles (regional peaks).

Throughput / SLA discussion (primary negotiation focus):
- Customer wants a firmed baseline throughput guarantee: 12,000 tokens/sec sustained across the dedicated pool during committed hours (08:00-20:00 PT), with 6,000 tokens/sec outside committed hours.
- Per-session concurrency: prefer per-session cap of 32 concurrent requests with P95 latency target. Global concurrency cap: 512 concurrent sessions for the tenant (can be sharded across GPU nodes).
- Burst policy ask: allow bursts up to 2.5x baseline for short windows (up to 10 minutes per hour) without surcharge; excess beyond burst to throttle or fall back to hosted model. PrismFlow wants 2 burst credits/hour retained.
- Latency SLOs: P95 <= 250ms for 512-token requests; P99 <= 400ms for same at baseline load. For 2048-token requests, agreed P95 <= 450ms best-effort, with fallback to a quantized variant if SLO would be violated.
- Min tokens/sec vs concurrency tradeoffs: they requested a written mapping table: e.g., baseline 12k tokens/sec == 512 global concurrency with avg 120 tokens/request. Need Redwood to provide a simple sizing table and worst-case headroom assumptions.
- Reserved GPU planning: PrismFlow expects to reserve initially 6 GPU equivalents (A100-40GB baseline) with option to scale to 10 within 90 days. They asked for node placement constraints (eu vs na) and burstable spare capacity across regions.
- SLA credits: heavy negotiation on credit formula. PrismFlow prefers % credits tied to sustained under-provisioning (not transient spikes). Legal flagged indemnity and data-residency clauses.
- Failover / fallback: request automatic fallback policy to a compatible smaller model hosted in Redwood if dedicated pool saturates; need clear routing policy and observed latency degradation thresholds that trigger fallback.

Customer quotes / paraphrases: "We need true predictability for our bidding window — if latency slips by 100ms we lose X% CTR." 

Cost sensitivity: Medium-high. Willing to commit to a 12-month reserved contract if throughput guarantees + credits are tight. Procurement wants clear uplift pricing for burst and overage.

Requested artifacts from Redwood:
- Written throughput-to-concurrency sizing table (by model family & token length).
- Draft SLA appendix with credit calc for sustained underperformance and burst policy language.
- Network baseline test slot (1 hour) with guide and contact.
- KMS/HSM integration runbook and timeline.

- SE/Marco to produce sizing table + annotated assumptions by 2026-03-10.
